fingerprint.session: CachyOS/KDE Plasma 6 Wayland, RS3 NXT via XWayland
fingerprint._note: Regions are pixel offsets measured on this exact window size. At any other size they resolve elsewhere and fail silently - OCR returns nothing, or reads a neighbouring panel. ui_scale 1.75 is the logical-to-physical factor KWin reports (2194 logical vs 3840 pixels); `doctor` detects it independently and reports it.

window._comment: RS3 NXT. WM_CLASS survives title changes and skips the Steam launcher window.

_profile_note: Basic Woodcutting profile: three alerts only - pack about to fill, chopping stopped, and the one-hour session milestone. Regions are reused verbatim from the fishing profile, which is safe because RS3 pins these panels to the window edges at a fixed size: the backpack, chat and Metrics panel sit in exactly the same place whatever skill is being trained. Verified here rather than assumed - `doctor` resolves every region and the occupancy grid was checked against the live pack.
_regions_help: anchor + dx,dy offset from that corner + fixed w,h. RS3 pins panels to edges at fixed size rather than scaling them, so this survives a window resize. Negative dx/dy measure inward from a right/bottom edge.

chat_tail._note: Most recent ~32 lines of All Chat. Taken from the thieving profile rather than fishing's smaller box: woodcutting produces a log line roughly every 2-3s, so the taller region gives each line many more chances to be read before it scrolls off. dy=-36 is the largest offset that still excludes the chat input bar below it; at -57 the boundary falls mid-line and the NEWEST message - the one rules care about most - OCRs as garbage.

backpack._note: Full backpack panel; grid is relative to the region's top-left. VERIFIED live while chopping maples: per-cell occupancy signal read 21-47 for slots holding logs and 0.8-4.1 for empty ones, so the threshold of 8 sits far from both populations. The grid describes 5x6=30 cells while the pack holds 28; the two surplus cells are always empty and are simply never counted as occupied.

gold_row._note: The Metrics panel's gold row: Gain, Drops and GP/h, left to right. MEASURED live while cutting acadia - OCR returns '523,692 0 2,438,927' and the Gain column climbs monotonically. dy=270, NOT the boss profile's 240: woodcutting shows fewer XP rows above, so the row sits lower, and at 240 this region lands on the 'Gain Drops GP/h' header and returns no numbers. Found by scanning dy=250..320; 270 was the only offset giving a clean three-number row with no header bleed. Re-measure with `shot gold_row` if the Metrics panel is reconfigured - this offset does not transfer between profiles.

session_timer._note: Elapsed-time readout at the bottom of the Metrics panel, between the settings/reset buttons on the left and pause on the right. Same geometry as every other profile - RS3 pins the panel top-left at a fixed size. Re-check with `shot session_timer` if the Metrics panel is moved or resized.

rules.name: pack_nearly_full
rules._wood_box_note: min_occupancy exists because of the Magic wood box. Clicking it stores logs in batches, so the pack empties mid-grind without any banking - MEASURED live: occupancy ran 7 -> 1 -> 7 -> 2 -> 10 -> 20 inside 50 seconds. The evaluator treats any drop of more than 2 slots as a bank trip and clears the fill-rate history, so the rapid gains straight after a box store look like an explosive fill rate. Replaying that exact sequence through the rule fired '18 slots left - bank soon' at 10/28 and then disarmed itself all the way to 27/28: it cried wolf early and was silent when the pack really was about to fill. Requiring 18 occupied before a PROJECTION may fire turns that into a correct warning at 20/28 with 8 slots left. warn_free=3 is unaffected - it reads the live count, which is true whatever the history says, so a genuine near-full pack still alerts even if the projection is suppressed.
rules._alert_body_note: No alert_body on purpose. The evaluator builds its own message when the projection fires - '{free} slots left, filling at {rate}/min - full in ~{eta}s' - which is the fishing-style fill-rate text. Setting alert_body here overrides that and throws the rate away, which is what this rule did until the rate was asked for explicitly.
rules._note: Advance warning: fires when the projected time-to-full drops below lead_seconds, so it arrives while there is still time to act rather than after chopping has already stopped. lead_seconds=20 and warn_free=3 against a measured log rate of roughly one every 2-3s - three free slots is about 6-9 seconds of chopping, so the projection and the slot floor agree with each other. Deliberately paired with nothing: the fishing and thieving profiles also carry an 'overflow' backstop rule, but this is a basic profile and two inventory alerts per bank trip is the noise problem those profiles had to be retuned away from. If a full pack is being missed, add an overflow rule rather than lowering lead_seconds.

rules.name: woodcutting_stopped
rules.suppress_pattern: backpack .?s too full|w[o0a][o0]d ?box .{0,4}s (now |too )?full|can'?t carry any more|do not have any space in your inventory|not have any space
rules.alert_body: No logs for {quiet:.0f}s - chopping has stopped.
rules._note: Fires when all evidence of chopping stops - the tree was felled, the pack filled, or the character was moved. VERIFIED against live chat while cutting maples: the two real lines are 'You get some maple logs.' and 'You swing your hatchet at the tree.'. The 'g?' in 'you g?et' is NOT a typo. MEASURED over 852 live lines: tesseract drops the g and reads 'You et some maple logs' often enough that the strict spelling matched only 71% of them, while 'you g?et some \w+ logs' reached 90% and adding the hatchet line covered 100%. A rule that misses three lines in ten would keep declaring a stop mid-chop. The tree name is '[\w ]{1,20}?', NOT '\w+'. Moving from maples to acadia broke the rule outright: the line is 'You get some acadia TREE logs', two words before 'logs', so a single-token match failed on every acadia log and only 1-4 of 31 chat lines matched. The lazy quantifier with a length cap allows multi-word names ('eternal magic tree') while still refusing to run across a whole sentence, which is what kept 'You have earned 92 sentinel fragments...' and the news broadcasts out. Checked against nine real non-activity lines. suppress_pattern is essential for the same reason it is in the fishing profile: a full pack halts chopping outright, so log messages stop on EVERY bank trip - without it this rule fires once per trip, which is exactly the once-per-cycle noise the other profiles had to be retuned to avoid. pack_nearly_full already reports that case. stop_seconds=45 against a log arriving every 2-3s leaves a very wide margin for a garbled OCR run; lower it to ~20 if a faster stop report matters more than tolerance for unreadable frames.

rules.name: pack_full
rules.pattern: backpack .?s too full|can'?t carry any more \w+
rules.alert_body: Backpack is full - chopping has stopped.
rules._note: The backstop pack_nearly_full cannot be: it reports the pack ALREADY full, which is the point at which chopping has actually halted. Chat-driven rather than a second 'inventory' rule, because the game says so explicitly and a chat line needs no fill-rate history - the wood box wrecks that history, which is the whole reason min_occupancy exists on the predictive rule. VERIFIED live while cutting acadia: 'Your backpack is too full to hold anything more.' appeared 26 times in 75 seconds of a full pack. The pattern writes 'backpack .?s too full' because tesseract drops the i and renders 'backpack s too full' - observed 13 times against 11 clean reads, so nearly half. Deliberately does NOT match 'Your wood box is now full', which is a different event: the box filling is not the pack filling, and the two were checked against each other. cooldown=90 because the game repeats this line on every further chop attempt - without it this fires several times a second.

rules.name: wood_box_full
rules.alert_body: The wood box is full - it will not absorb any more logs.
rules._note: A full wood box is the moment the pack starts filling for real: until then the box quietly absorbs logs, which is why occupancy oscillates instead of climbing. Knowing the box is full explains why the next bank warning arrives so much sooner. TWO verified phrasings, both seen live: 'Your wood box is now full. It stores all items from the backpack.' and 'Your wood box is too full to deposit all items from the backpack.' The second was found only by re-reading live chat after the first pattern was written - a pattern anchored on 'is now full' would have missed it entirely. Hence '(now |too )?full'. The character classes absorb the usual OCR damage on this line (Vourwood, biox); frames where the word 'box' itself is destroyed are still missed, which is acceptable for an informational alert that repeats. cooldown=300 because it is a once-per-trip event.

rules.name: birds_nest
rules.pattern: bird'?s nest|a nest falls out of the tree|nest falls
rules.alert_body: A bird's nest dropped - pick it up before it disappears.
rules._note: UNVERIFIED WORDING - treat as probably wrong until a nest actually drops and the line is read. Per the RuneScape Wiki, nests fall TO THE GROUND rather than into the backpack, which is why this watches chat rather than the inventory grid, and why the alert says to pick it up: an unnoticed nest is simply lost. The wiki documents the drop and its sound effect but does not quote the chat line, so the alternatives here are a guess covering the likely phrasings. Four of five patterns guessed this way in earlier profiles were wrong when finally checked against live chat - see docs/validation-session-2026-09-21.md. Short cooldown because nests are rare and each one matters. Confirm and tighten on the first real drop.

rules.name: impling
rules.pattern: a creature is discovered while skilling|an impling (has )?appear
rules.alert_body: An impling appeared - catch it before it despawns.
rules._note: The first alternative is VERIFIED from live chat during fishing ('A creature is discovered while skilling'), which is the wording RS3 uses for a skilling impling spawn; the second is a defensive guess kept from the fishing profile. Implings spawn silently and despawn, so the message is easy to miss mid-grind, and the long timeout keeps the popup on screen long enough to be seen on a glance. Enabled here on the strength of the fishing verification - the line is a property of skilling, not of the skill - but it has NOT been seen during woodcutting specifically.

rules.name: gold_milestone
rules._note: Reads the Gain column of the Metrics panel's gold row and fires once per million. MEASURED live: the row OCRs as '523,692 0 2,438,927' (Gain, Drops, GP/h) and parse_total correctly takes the first number, climbing monotonically 523,692 -> 534,882 across six samples three seconds apart. dy=270 rather than the boss profile's 240: the woodcutting Metrics panel shows fewer XP rows, so the gold row sits lower, and at 240 the region lands on the 'Gain Drops GP/h' HEADER and returns no numbers at all. Scanned dy=250..320 to find it - 270 was the only offset returning a clean three-number row with no header bleed. This is the same class of error as the boss profile's original 320: a gold row offset cannot be carried between profiles, it has to be measured per layout.

rules.name: session_hour
rules._note: Reads the Metrics panel's own elapsed timer rather than tracking wall-clock time in the watcher. That is the better source: it is the number already on screen, it pauses when the player pauses it, and it survives a watcher restart because the game owns it. step=3600 fires once per hour. The parser anchors on [0-5] for the minute and second fields so a garbled frame like '00:82:09' is rejected rather than becoming a bogus elapsed time, and a timer reset rewinds the milestone counter so a fresh session starts clean.

_notification_note: Rules use urgency 'normal' with an explicit timeout_ms so KDE auto-dismisses them. Setting urgency to 'critical' makes KDE keep the popup until it is closed by hand and ignore timeout_ms - only do that for an alert you must not miss.
